title: Name the relationship first
hook: Ignore the choices. Read the sentences on both sides and say how they connect: same way, opposite way, or cause and effect.

steps.prompt: Sort each transition by the relationship it signals.
steps.why: Learn these three families and most transition questions take seconds.

steps.prompt: 'Penguins can't fly. ______ they are excellent swimmers.'
steps.why: Swimming is what they do in place of flying.

steps.prompt: 'The library extended its weekend hours. ______ more students studied there on weekends.'
steps.why: More students is the effect of longer hours.

steps.prompt: Two choices mean almost the same thing, like 'therefore' and 'thus.' What does that usually tell you?
steps.answer: Neither is likely the answer, since there can only be one right choice.

steps.prompt: 'The novel was rejected by twelve publishers. ______ it became a bestseller.'
Match each sentence pair to its best transition.
left: It rained all day. The game was canceled.
Cats sleep a lot. Dogs nap often too.
The plan was cheap. It failed anyway.
Many fruits have seeds. Strawberries carry theirs outside.
steps.why: Cause, similarity, contrast, example: name it first, then pick.

keys: Name the relationship before reading choices.
Three families: same direction, opposite direction, cause and effect.
Choices that mean the same thing are usually both wrong.

recall.prompt: 'Coral reefs cover under one percent of the ocean floor. ______ they hold a quarter of marine species.'
recall.why: Small area versus huge diversity is a contrast.

recall.prompt: What do you do before reading transition choices?
recall.answer: Name the relationship between the two sentences.
